topics.title: Management of e-Waste
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The students should be able to state the meaning of e-waste, list sources of e-waste in Nigeria, explain safe disposal methods, and identify environmental effects of improper e-waste management.
Introduction:
We have learned about different types of electronic devices in our previous lessons. Today we will discuss what happens to these devices when they are no longer useful.
Content:
e-Waste means electronic waste like old phones, computers, and TVs. Sources include homes, offices, and schools. In Nigeria, many people have old phones they no longer use. Safe disposal methods include recycling centers, proper collection points, and manufacturer take-back programs. For example, MTN has collection centers for old phones. Environmental effects include soil and water pollution from toxic materials like lead and mercury, which can harm our health and farming.
Class activity:
Students will work in groups to identify e-waste items in their homes and suggest proper disposal methods for each.
Evaluation questions:
1. What is e-Waste?
2. List two sources of e-Waste in Nigeria.
3. Explain one safe disposal method for e-Waste.
4. How does improper e-Waste disposal affect our environment?
Summary:
Proper management of e-Waste is important to protect our environment and health.

topics.title: Recycling Digital Devices
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The students should be able to define recycling of digital devices, list steps in refurbishing old gadgets, and explain benefits of reusing electronic devices.
Introduction:
Last week we learned about e-Waste management. Today we will focus on how we can recycle and reuse old digital devices instead of throwing them away.
Content:
Recycling digital devices means processing old electronics to make new products or refurbish them for reuse. Steps include collecting devices, testing them, repairing faults, upgrading parts, and reselling or donating them. For example, old laptops can be upgraded with more memory and given to schools in rural areas. Benefits include reducing waste, saving money, and creating jobs. In Nigeria, some organizations collect old phones, repair them, and sell them at lower prices to people who cannot afford new ones.
Class activity:
Students will bring old phones or gadgets if available and learn basic refurbishing steps like cleaning and replacing simple parts.
Evaluation questions:
1. What does recycling digital devices mean?
2. List three steps in refurbishing old gadgets.
3. Explain two benefits of reusing electronic devices.
4. How can recycling help Nigerian communities?
Summary:
Recycling and reusing digital devices helps reduce waste and provides affordable technology to more people.

topics.title: Emerging Technologies
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The students should be able to define IoT, Cloud, Blockchain, and AR/VR, list examples of each technology in Nigeria, and explain their importance.
Introduction:
We have studied many digital technologies so far. Today we will learn about new technologies that are becoming popular around the world including in Nigeria.
Content:
IoT means Internet of Things - devices connected to the internet like smart home systems. In Nigeria, some people use smart irrigation systems for their farms. Cloud computing means storing and accessing data online instead of on your computer. Many Nigerian businesses use Google Drive or Microsoft 365. Blockchain is a secure way of recording transactions like cryptocurrencies. Some Nigerian startups use blockchain for payment systems. AR/VR means Augmented Reality and Virtual Reality - technologies that create digital worlds or add digital elements to our world. Some Nigerian universities use VR for teaching.
Class activity:
Students will research one emerging technology and present how it could be used in a Nigerian context.
Evaluation questions:
1. What does IoT stand for?
2. Explain Cloud computing with an example.
3. How can Blockchain be used in Nigeria?
4. What is the difference between AR and VR?
Summary:
Emerging technologies are changing how we live and work in Nigeria and around the world.

topics.title: Preparing for Digital Future
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The students should be able to explain the importance of STEM education, list career pathways in digital technologies, and identify skills needed for future jobs.
Introduction:
As we approach the end of junior secondary school, it is important to think about our future careers and how digital technologies will be part of them.
Content:
STEM means Science, Technology, Engineering, and Mathematics. These subjects are important for careers in digital technologies. In Nigeria, many jobs now require digital skills like programming, data analysis, and cybersecurity. Career pathways include software development, digital marketing, IT support, and data science. For example, a student interested in computers could learn programming languages like Python and work for Nigerian tech companies like Andela or Flutterwave. Skills needed include problem-solving, creativity, and continuous learning as technology changes quickly.
Class activity:
Students will create a career plan that includes STEM subjects and digital skills they want to develop.
Evaluation questions:
1. What does STEM stand for?
2. List two career pathways in digital technologies.
3. Explain why digital skills are important in Nigeria today.
4. What skills do you need to prepare for future digital jobs?
Summary:
Developing STEM knowledge and digital skills will help students succeed in Nigeria's growing digital economy.

topics.title: MID-TERM TEST
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The students should be able to demonstrate understanding of topics covered in weeks 1-4 through written assessment.
Introduction:
Today we will have our mid-term test to check how well you have learned the topics we have covered so far this term.
Content:
The test will cover Management of e-Waste, Recycling Digital Devices, Emerging Technologies, and Preparing for Digital Future. Questions will include definitions, examples, and explanations related to these topics. Students should review their class notes and previous evaluation questions to prepare.
Class activity:
Students will complete a written test covering the first four weeks of the term.
Evaluation questions:
The test will contain multiple choice, short answer, and essay questions covering all topics from weeks 1-4.
Summary:
The mid-term test will help students and teacher identify areas of strength and weakness for further study.

topics.title: Artificial Intelligence in Everyday Life
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The students should be able to define Artificial Intelligence, list examples of AI in Nigeria, explain how AI works in daily applications, and discuss benefits and challenges of AI.
Introduction:
We have learned about emerging technologies. Today we will focus specifically on Artificial Intelligence, which is becoming more common in our daily lives in Nigeria.
Content:
Artificial Intelligence (AI) means computer systems that can perform tasks usually requiring human intelligence. Examples in Nigeria include voice assistants like Google Assistant on smartphones, recommendation systems on Jumia or Konga, and chatbots for customer service. AI works by learning from large amounts of data using algorithms. For example, Netflix recommends shows based on what you have watched before. Benefits include faster service, personalized experiences, and solving complex problems. Challenges include job displacement and ethical concerns about privacy.
Class activity:
Students will use voice assistants on their phones or in the computer lab to experience AI applications and discuss how they work.
Evaluation questions:
1. What is Artificial Intelligence?
2. List two examples of AI used in Nigeria.
3. How does a recommendation system like Jumia's work?
4. What are two benefits of AI in daily life?
5. What is one challenge of AI technology?
Summary:
AI is becoming part of our everyday lives in Nigeria and understanding how it works helps us use it better.

topics.title: MID-TERM BREAK
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The students should be able to rest and prepare for the second half of the term.
Introduction:
After several weeks of hard work, it is time for a break to rest and recharge.
Content:
Mid-term break is a time for students to rest, spend time with family, and prepare for the remaining weeks of the term. Students should use this time to review what they have learned so far and complete any assignments. Teachers will also use this time to prepare for the next topics.
Class activity:
No formal class activity during break period. Students are encouraged to rest and engage in safe recreational activities.
Evaluation questions:
No formal evaluation during break period.
Summary:
Enjoy your break and return refreshed for the second half of the term.

topics.title: Global Digital Citizenship
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The students should be able to define digital citizenship, list responsibilities of digital citizens, explain ethical issues in digital world, and identify ways to stay safe online.
Introduction:
As we use digital technologies more in our daily lives, it is important to understand how to be responsible citizens in the digital world.
Content:
Digital citizenship means responsible use of technology and online participation. Responsibilities include respecting others online, protecting personal information, and following laws. Ethical issues include cyberbullying, fake news, and online fraud. In Nigeria, many people have experienced scams through SMS or social media. Ways to stay safe include using strong passwords, verifying information before sharing, and reporting inappropriate content. For example, if someone sends you a message asking for bank details, you should not respond and tell an adult.
Class activity:
Students will create posters about digital citizenship and online safety to display in the classroom.
Evaluation questions:
1. What is digital citizenship?
2. List two responsibilities of digital citizens.
3. Explain what cyberbullying is and how to prevent it.
4. How can you protect your personal information online?
5. What should you do if you encounter fake news?
Summary:
Being a good digital citizen means using technology responsibly and safely in our connected world.

topics.title: Technology and Sustainable Development
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The students should be able to define sustainable development, list SDGs related to technology, explain how ICT helps achieve SDGs, and identify examples in Nigeria.
Introduction:
We have learned about many digital technologies. Today we will explore how these technologies can help achieve sustainable development goals in Nigeria and around the world.
Content:
Sustainable development means meeting our needs without compromising future generations. The Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) are 17 global goals including no poverty, quality education, and climate action. SDGs related to technology include SDG 9 (industry, innovation, and infrastructure) and SDG 13 (climate action). ICT helps achieve these goals by improving access to information, enabling remote work, and optimizing resource use. In Nigeria, mobile banking helps achieve SDG 1 (no poverty) by providing financial services to rural areas. Solar-powered computers in schools help achieve SDG 4 (quality education) in areas without electricity.
Class activity:
Students will research one Nigerian initiative that uses technology to achieve an SDG and present their findings.
Evaluation questions:
1. What is sustainable development?
2. List two SDGs related to technology.
3. Explain how ICT helps achieve SDG 4 (quality education).
4. Give one example of technology being used for sustainable development in Nigeria.
Summary:
Digital technologies play an important role in achieving sustainable development goals in Nigeria.

topics.title: Final Project: Student Digital Innovation
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The students should be able to design a digital solution to a local problem, create a prototype or presentation, and demonstrate their project to the class.
Introduction:
Throughout this term, we have learned about various digital technologies and their applications. Today we will apply this knowledge by creating our own digital innovations.
Content:
For the final project, students will work individually or in groups to identify a problem in their community, school, or home and design a digital solution. The solution could be an app, website, device, or system that addresses the problem. Students should research their problem, brainstorm solutions, create a prototype or presentation, and prepare to demonstrate their project. For example, a group might design an app to help farmers in their area get market information for their produce, or a system to reduce electricity waste in the school.
Class activity:
Students will work on their projects throughout the week, with teacher guidance, and present their final projects on Friday.
Evaluation questions:
1. What problem did your project address?
2. What digital solution did you design?
3. How will your solution help the community?
4. What challenges did you face while creating your project?
Summary:
This project allows students to apply their digital knowledge to create real-world solutions.

topics.title: REVISION
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The students should be able to review and consolidate knowledge from the entire term, identify areas of weakness, and prepare for final examination.
Introduction:
As we approach the end of the term, it is important to review all the topics we have covered to prepare for our final examination.
Content:
Revision will cover all topics from the term including Management of e-Waste, Recycling Digital Devices, Emerging Technologies, Preparing for Digital Future, Artificial Intelligence, Global Digital Citizenship, Technology and Sustainable Development, and the Digital Innovation Project. Students should focus on understanding key concepts, definitions, examples, and applications. Areas of weakness identified during mid-term test should receive special attention. Teachers will provide review materials and practice questions to help students prepare.
Class activity:
Students will participate in group revision sessions, create mind maps of key topics, and complete practice questions.
Evaluation questions:
Revision questions will cover all topics from the term to help students prepare for the final examination.
Summary:
Thorough revision will help students perform well in their final examination.

topics.title: EXAMINATION
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The students should be able to demonstrate their knowledge and understanding of Digital Technologies through completion of the final examination.
Introduction:
Today you will write your final examination for Digital Technologies. This will assess your understanding of all topics covered this term.
Content:
The examination will cover all topics from the term including Management of e-Waste, Recycling Digital Devices, Emerging Technologies, Preparing for Digital Future, Artificial Intelligence, Global Digital Citizenship, Technology and Sustainable Development, and the Digital Innovation Project. Questions will include multiple choice, short answer, and essay questions. Students should read all questions carefully and manage their time wisely. The examination will test both recall and application of knowledge.
Class activity:
Students will complete the final examination under examination conditions.
Evaluation questions:
The examination will contain questions covering all topics from the term.
Summary:
The final examination will provide a comprehensive assessment of students' learning in Digital Technologies for this term.

topics.title: CLOSING/VACATION
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The students should be able to reflect on their learning, complete end-of-term activities, and prepare for the vacation.
Introduction:
As we conclude this term of Digital Technologies, let's reflect on what we have learned and prepare for the vacation period.
Content:
The closing week involves returning textbooks, completing remaining assignments, and reflecting on learning experiences. Students should think about what they have learned about digital technologies and how they can apply this knowledge in the future. Teachers will provide feedback on student performance and suggestions for continued learning during the vacation. Students are encouraged to explore digital resources safely and continue developing their digital skills.
Class activity:
Students will participate in a reflection activity where they share their favorite topic from the term and one skill they have developed.
Evaluation questions:
No formal evaluation during closing week.
Summary:
The term has ended successfully, and students should use the vacation to rest and continue learning about digital technologies.
